criteria.criterion: crates/athena-testkit/Cargo.toml exists as a std-only dev-dependency crate with a workspace [lints] table, and is a workspace member in Cargo.toml. CHANGELOG.md names the root cause: executable stand-ins written in-process with no single helper and no mechanical enumeration of write sites. It also names the fix at the origin: athena_testkit::write_executable, which writes via an sh child (cat > tmp && chmod 755 tmp && mv tmp final).
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. crates/athena-testkit/Cargo.toml has an empty [dependencies], only tempfile under [dev-dependencies], and `[lints] workspace = true`. `cargo tree -e normal` prints only athena-testkit itself, so it uses std only. Root Cargo.toml adds it to `members` and to `[workspace.dependencies]`. Every consumer (xtask, athena-cli, athena-agent, athena-core, athena-git) takes it under [dev-dependencies] only. The policy test passes. The CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed entry gives the root cause in the criterion's terms and names the fix `athena_testkit::write_executable` via an sh child running `cat > tmp && chmod 755 tmp && mv tmp final`.

findings.summary: The scan matches text line by line, so some in-process write forms get past it.
findings.evidence: Five forms are missed: a `Command::new(` whose `"chmod"` argument is on the next line, `std::fs::copy` of an existing executable (copy keeps the mode and writes in-process), a call inside a /* */ block comment or a string literal, and `use std::fs::set_permissions as sp` aliasing. A syn-based pass (syn is already a workspace dependency) or one more `fs::copy(` pattern would close most of these. The approach matches the repository's existing text-scan convention (xtask/tests/policy.rs), and D160's Tradeoff states the limit, so this is not a blocker.

findings.summary: The test region begins at the first `#[cfg(test)]` line, so production code after an earlier cfg(test) item would be scanned as test code.
findings.evidence: `test_region_start` returns the first matching line, and everything after it counts as test code. This errs toward false positives (it fails loudly, not silently), and the current tree passes.

summary: The change passes. It moves the anti-ETXTBSY helper (the fix for flaky "Text file busy" test failures) into a new crate, athena-testkit, which uses only std and is a dev-dependency only. It converts the remaining in-process stand-in write, slot_exec.rs's fake cargo, and repoints every former script_writer caller. It removes the retry workaround in reading.rs's check_stub and adds a text scan, `no_in_process_exec_writes`, with planted-violation tests. All 25 changed files are on the deliverables list. I ran `cargo test -p athena-testkit` and all 14 tests passed. The stress test showed 0 busy-file errors in 800 cycles for the helper, against 15 in 800 for the in-process control on this host. The decisions, ci_shards and architecture-policy tests also passed. fmt, clippy and the full test suite come from Athena's recorded CI results, all passing. There are two small findings, neither blocking: the line-based scan misses some forms, such as a multi-line chmod Command or fs::copy of an existing executable, and it treats everything after the first #[cfg(test)] as test code.
